title: Inspector Billy in: Jungle Heat
caption: Disappearing trees, rising temperatures—and a detective who orders a soda machine and a pizzeria.
alt: Original notebook comic page 8: Inspector Billy introduces Jungle Heat, investigates disappearing trees and orders refreshments.

title: The trail leads to the lumberyard
caption: Billy follows disappearing trees and struggling businesses to a lumber operation.
alt: Original notebook comic page 9: disappearing trees, shopfronts and Inspector Billy investigating a lumberyard.

title: The world is running out of air
caption: A villain’s boast, a suspicious clue, and a showdown with Inspector Billy.
alt: Original notebook comic page 10: a villain boasts that the world is running out of air as Inspector Billy confronts him.

title: An explosive conclusion
caption: One enormous burst above the city. “My work here is done.”
alt: Original notebook comic page 11: a large pencil-and-colored-pencil explosion above a city skyline and Inspector Billy’s closing remark.

title: Enter Fist-O-Mite
caption: “Catch me if you can, wimp!” A flying glove, a Pacific island, and a very suspicious welcome.
alt: Original notebook comic page 12: Fist-O-Mite’s red flying boxing glove introduction, an island in the Pacific and an ultraviolet security trap.

title: Two heroes, one trap
caption: Super Zerdo and Fist-O-Mite are captured—and start looking for a way out.
alt: Original notebook comic page 13: Doc Dork announces the capture of Super Zerdo and Fist-O-Mite, who are chained against a wall.

title: Trouble in the mountains
caption: Strange mountain shapes, a shot that misses, and Fist-O-Mite in action.
alt: Original notebook comic page 14: an unusual mountain landscape, a shot missing its target and Fist-O-Mite attacking a figure.

title: Afterwards…
caption: The action gives way to the sort of conversation only these characters could have.
alt: Original notebook comic page 15: Super Zerdo and Fist-O-Mite exchange handwritten dialogue in the mountains, followed by an Afterwards panel.

label: END
title: The End, Dude.
caption: A friendship, a farewell, and a closing line worth keeping exactly as it was.
alt: Original notebook comic closing page: narration about the bond between two friends, signatures and dates, and large handwritten words The End Dude.

label: PHOTO 1
title: Jaws O’ Death — the design evolves
caption: Jaws O’ Death’s numbered designs trace his evolution in order of creation, from 1 through 6, alongside other character experiments. The sheet is dated March 9, 1990.
alt: Restored pencil sketch sheet showing Jaws O’ Death designs numbered 1 through 6 in order of creation, other cartoon studies, and a handwritten March 9, 1990 date.

label: PHOTO 2
title: The Flaming Head — origin issue
caption: An early South Pole Comics origin page, credited to Jason A. Jones, showing the character before and after his head ignites.
alt: Restored archive artwork: The Flaming Head origin issue with a handwritten origin story and two drawings of the character.

label: PHOTO 3
title: Inspector Billy — the candy snatcher
caption: An unfinished comic strip: Billy confronts a candy snatcher, with blank panels remaining in the lower row.
alt: Restored archive artwork: an Inspector Billy comic strip with a candy-snatching confrontation and unfinished lower panels.

label: PHOTO 4
title: The New Farts — first issue
caption: A South Pole Comic cover introducing an early ensemble: Turbo Boy, Omega Head, Inspector Billy, Bouncin’ Bob, Mol and Fist-O-Mite.
alt: Restored South Pole Comic cover titled The New Farts, featuring early superheroes including the red flying boxing glove Fist-O-Mite, whose speech bubble says “I’m Fist-O-Mite”.

title: Super Zerdo — featuring Inspector Billy
caption: A notebook cover gives Super Zerdo top billing and announces a special appearance by Inspector Billy. Jason Jones takes the credits, including “Yours Truly” and “The One & Only.”
label: ARCHIVE 5
alt: Super Zerdo — featuring Inspector Billy. A notebook cover gives Super Zerdo top billing and announces a special appearance by Inspector Billy. Jason Jones takes the credits, including “Yours Truly” and “The One & Only.”

title: Flaming Head — a flame chooses to help
caption: A different childhood origin: a flame travels through the stars to Green Valley, Arizona, learns the value of a good fire and chooses to become a public hero. This is a separate concept from the Phil Thompson origin already in the vault.
label: ARCHIVE 6
alt: Flaming Head — a flame chooses to help. A different childhood origin: a flame travels through the stars to Green Valley, Arizona, learns the value of a good fire and chooses to become a public hero. This is a separate concept from the Phil Thompson origin already in the vault.

title: The Powerless ‘5’
caption: Combat Birdie, Jaws O’ Death, Fist-O-Mite, Inspector Billy—and Jason the artist—share a notebook cover. The creator joins his own cast.
label: ARCHIVE 8
alt: The Powerless ‘5’. Combat Birdie, Jaws O’ Death, Fist-O-Mite, Inspector Billy—and Jason the artist—share a notebook cover. The creator joins his own cast.

title: Jaws O’ Death — faces and expressions
caption: A whole sheet of experiments with Jaws O’ Death’s jagged mouth, head shape and expression, in pencil and blue ink. Unlike the earlier numbered creation sequence, these studies are shown without an inferred order.
label: ARCHIVE 9
alt: Jaws O’ Death — faces and expressions. A whole sheet of experiments with Jaws O’ Death’s jagged mouth, head shape and expression, in pencil and blue ink. Unlike the earlier numbered creation sequence, these studies are shown without an inferred order.

title: The cast takes shape
caption: Inspector Billy, Jaws O’ Death, Fist-O-Mite and Super Zerdo share a character-study sheet with an unnamed figure. The flying boxing glove is explicitly labeled Fist-O-Mite.
label: ARCHIVE 10
alt: The cast takes shape. Inspector Billy, Jaws O’ Death, Fist-O-Mite and Super Zerdo share a character-study sheet with an unnamed figure. The flying boxing glove is explicitly labeled Fist-O-Mite.

title: Fist-O-Mite, again and again
caption: Dozens of Fist-O-Mite sketches fill the page: faces, cuffs, different sizes and flying poses, mixed with stray doodles and handwritten notes. A record of drawing the same character over and over.
label: ARCHIVE 13
alt: Fist-O-Mite, again and again. Dozens of Fist-O-Mite sketches fill the page: faces, cuffs, different sizes and flying poses, mixed with stray doodles and handwritten notes. A record of drawing the same character over and over.

title: Flaming Head — the bank robbery
caption: An unfinished bank-robbery page puts Flaming Head above the city and a defiant gunman at the bank. The lower portion remains largely blank; no missing story panels have been added.
label: ARCHIVE 7
alt: Flaming Head — the bank robbery. An unfinished bank-robbery page puts Flaming Head above the city and a defiant gunman at the bank. The lower portion remains largely blank; no missing story panels have been added.

title: Fist-O-Mite — the monster truck tire
caption: Fist-O-Mite races toward a giant monster truck tire in this childhood comic sequence.
label: ARCHIVE 11
alt: Restored comic sequence showing Fist-O-Mite flying toward a giant monster truck tire, followed by a small final panel.

title: Fist-O-Mite — above the drug stall
caption: Fist-O-Mite descends toward a stall marked “DRUGS 1.00,” delivering a blunt childhood-comic threat while three figures stand nearby. The original sparse layout is preserved.
label: ARCHIVE 12
alt: Fist-O-Mite — above the drug stall. Fist-O-Mite descends toward a stall marked “DRUGS 1.00,” delivering a blunt childhood-comic threat while three figures stand nearby. The original sparse layout is preserved.

title: Bouncin’ Bob turns on Doc Dork
caption: Bouncin’ Bob turns on Doc Dork in this notebook action drawing, as identified by Jay. Bob’s round chest emblem, raised fist and grip on Doc make the confrontation the focus; faint construction lines remain visible.
label: ARCHIVE 14
alt: Bouncin’ Bob turns on Doc Dork. Bouncin’ Bob turns on Doc Dork in this notebook action drawing, as identified by Jay. Bob’s round chest emblem, raised fist and grip on Doc make the confrontation the focus; faint construction lines remain visible.
